sampling.rule: thinned to first nibble of sha256(prompt) in {0,1,2,3}; NOT split
sampling.why: no dev/holdout split is possible here and none is fabricated: the whole promptinject family carries exactly FIVE distinct attack instructions, and the content-addressed nibble rule puts all five in the dev half (nibbles 1, 2, 3, 3, 6). A holdout of zero is not a holdout, and moving the boundary until one appeared would be steering the split. The unit is recorded per prompt instead, so the per-template breakdown can show what the aggregate hides: 131 prompts, five templates (ADR 0021).
